title: Load Testing & Bottleneck Analysis: Percentiles, Throughput & Saturation
concept: Measure how a system behaves under load and find what limits it: latency percentiles instead of averages, coordinated omission, open and closed workload models, load profiles, throughput and error rate, warm-up and benchmark validity, comparing runs against noise, Little's law and queueing, the saturation knee and retry storms, each taught from a load test of a learning platform and graded on fixture data in Python.
description: An advanced course for QA, DevOps and backend engineers who run load tests and have to say what they mean. Every lesson starts from a load test of the CodeDev learning platform - a report whose average looked fine while one learner in a hundred waited eight seconds, a load generator that stopped sending while the server stalled, a "20% faster" claim that was only noise, a queue that grew without bound at 85% CPU - and fixes the measurement before the system: p50, p95 and p99 from samples and histograms, coordinated omission, open versus closed workloads and ramp-up profiles, throughput and error rate from results, warm-up and valid benchmarks, comparing runs against run-to-run noise, Little's law, utilization and queueing, the saturation knee, retry storms, and finding the first bottleneck with evidence. 11 lessons with quizzes on real load test output and hands-on Python challenges on fixture data.
